newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp held talks to buy Amex - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp held talks to buy Amex - WSJ.

text.p: In what could have resulted in the largest acquisition in U.S. history, Citicorp held unsuccessful talks to acquire American Express beginning in November and ending last week, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
The talks were initiated by American Express Chairman Harvey Golub and involved Citicorp Chairman John Reed, the story says.

It is unclear how far the discussions progressed, though they apparently faltered on several issues, among them the likelihood that Citicorp would have to give up its affiliation with Visa and MasterCard in order to combine with American Express, the story says.

Though the talks are over, rumors of a possible Citicorp/American Express merger surfaced in financial markets in the past three days, contributing to unusually heavy volume in both stocks, the story says.
Citicorp declined to comment on the story while American Express said it was not engaged in discussions regarding sale of the company.
